The project is the Middle East's largest integrated leisure and theme park destination located on Sheikh Zayed road in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Chadi was assigned to my package The Riverland even though he is coming from EPC Oil and Gas environment he demonstrated great skills as Client Representative PMC managing various main contractors and consultants adopting a fast track multi-package strategy. The below scope of works covers Package I currently but will extend to Packages II and III as optional after agreement with the Client. The information for existing networks for dry and wet utilities has been obtained from the stakeholders/ service providers; however, the accuracy of the information needs to be validated to avoid unforeseen circumstances/ scenarios. # Fall Protection — Site Safety Criteria (OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart M) REAL, sourced fall-protection thresholds for construction sites. Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502 (Subpart M), US federal regulation, public domain. This is a US-reference standard: in Saudi Arabia site HSE is governed by Saudi labour law (MHRSD) and the project's approved HSE plan, not OSHA — but Saudi practice broadly aligns with these figures. Use as an engineering reference; enforce against the project HSE plan. Values are metric-led (SI) with the original US-customary figure, as written in the regulation, in parentheses. ## Guardrail systems## Guardrail systems | Parameter | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Top-rail height above walking surface | 1.1 m (± 8 cm) | 42 in (± 3 in) | | Top-rail minimum strength (force withstood) | 890 N | 200 lbf | | Maximum opening / midrail gap | 0.48 m | 19 in | | Toeboard minimum vertical height | 9 cm | 3½ in |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(b), (j). ## Personal fall arrest system (PFAS)## Personal fall arrest system (PFAS) | Parameter | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Maximum arresting force on the body (harness) | 8 kN | 1,800 lbf | | Maximum free-fall distance | 1.8 m | 6 ft | | Maximum deceleration distance | 1.07 m | 3½ ft | | Anchorage strength, per attached worker | 22.2 kN | 5,000 lbf |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(d). Note: anchorage may instead be part of a system designed and used under a qualified person's supervision at a safety factor of 2. ## Hole and opening covers Covers over holes must be capable of supporting at least twice the combined weight of workers, equipment, and materials that may be imposed on them (rated to 2x the imposed load), and must be secured and colour-coded or marked "HOLE" / "COVER". Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(i)."COVER". Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(i). ## KSA applicability OSHA 1926 is US federal site-safety law and is not the governing authority in Saudi Arabia. Site HSE in KSA is regulated under Saudi labour law (MHRSD) and the project's approved HSE/safety plan; SBC (Saudi Building Code) governs building design, not site safety. These thresholds are a US engineering reference. Saudi practice broadly aligns: guardrails ~1.0–1.1 m high, a 1.8 m free-fall limit, andls ~1.0–1.1 m high, a 1.8 m free-fall limit, and PFAS anchorage in the 22 kN range. Where a value is enforced on site, confirm it against the project HSE plan. ## How to use - Fall protection is generally required at a fall height of 1.8 m (6 ft) or more in construction (Subpart M general trigger, 1926.501). - Quote the SI value for site use; cite the US original and the regulation number so the basis is traceable. - State that this is a US-reference figure and that the project HSE plan / local regulation takes precedence where they differ. - Do not present OSHA as the legal authority for a Saudi project — it is a reference standard

Dear Sir, With reference to Contract DD-2023-118 for DGII-Infrastructure Package-1, Upon review of the Structural IFC drawings associated with the MV Culvert, the Contractor identified missing data as below listed: • Complete structural package design details drawings for MV culvert. • Two Culvert Intersection details. • Complete profile drawing for MV culvert. • Required design MEP services inside the culvert. with reference at (1), which has been answered by the Engineer under letter at reference (2) as follows: “The MV culvert is subject to SEC approval and agreement between DGCL and SEC. Details of the MV culvert will be issued to the Contractor as additional IFC drawings in due course.” Further, the Contractor has requested, under its letter at reference (3), to be provided with a complete SEC approved structural package to carry out the required and necessary coordination with other utilities. The same was replied by the Engineer on March 07, 2024, under letter at reference (4) as follows: “We note below with respect to the specific details being requested: 1. Discussions are ongoing between SEC and DGCL regarding the MV Culvert. Grounds how the platform reasons about disciplines, coordination, and clash/interface issues. ## The major systems## The major systems | System | Function | Key interfaces | |---|---|---| | Building envelope | Separates interior from exterior; controls heat, air, moisture, water | Structure (support), HVAC (loads) | | Structural | Carries and transfers loads to the ground; foundations, frame, floors, roof | Envelope, MEP penetrations | | HVAC / mechanical | Heating, ventilation, air conditioning — comfort and indoor air quality | Electrical (power), envelope (loads), controls | | Electrical | Power distribution, lighting, low-voltage/data | Every powered system | | Plumbing | Potable water supply, sanitary drainage, storm drainage | Structure (routing), fire protection | | Fire protection | Detection, alarm, suppression (sprinklers), and life-safety egress | Structure, electrical, HVAC (smoke control) | | Vertical transportation | Elevators, escalators, lifts | Structure (shafts), electrical | | Controls / BMS | Building management system integrating HVAC, lighting, energy, safety | All monitored systems |Source: WBDG design disciplines / building systems. ## Integration and coordination - The systems are **interdependent** — an envelope decision changes HVAC loads; a structural change moves MEP routing. Design is an **integrated** process, and most construction clashes are interface problems between these systems. - The **building envelope** is the primary control layer for energy and moisture; it is the single biggest lever on operational cost and comfort.le biggest lever on operational cost and comfort. - **Fire protection and life safety** cut across structure, electrical, HVAC (smoke control), and egress — treat them as a system, not one trade. ## How to use - Use this to explain what each system does and where systems interface (the usual source of coordination/clash issues — see the BIM reference note on clash detection). - The project specifications and the governing code/standard are authoritative for a specific design — this is the general framework.

Un-occupied Work Areas Where WAN’s have been issued to the Contractor it has taken on average 30 working days to develop the respective working plan and permit applications to initiate the works – this is consistent and unacceptable. Attachment 1 outlines the number of WAN areas where no works are proceeding to date. (some key data required here) In-sufficient Resources at Working Areas Ref Boulevard – B3 Wk 64 Actual Storm Water Pipework installed 100m in a typical week with one crew and a single crane. The issued program dictates 300m per week which requires at least 2 more crews. (ref Attachment 2 – Boulevard Program Extract) Ref Boulevard – B4 No activity of Storm Water installation in section B4 despite 70% of the area available for the last 3 working weeks. Detailed Design Report Package 1 IP-INF-054-0000-JCB-RPT-DE-000013-A 29 Value Engineering 29.1 General As part of the DGII infrastructure design delivery process, value engineering study is an integral part of the design development process. The VE study process defines a sequence of activities that are undertaken during a VE study; before, during, and following a workshop. During the VE workshop, the VE team learns about the background issues, defines and classifies the project functions, identifies creative approaches to provide the functions, and then evaluates, develops, and presents the VE proposals to key decision makers. The VE methodology consists of seven sequential phases as depicted in Figure 29-1: below. Those are information, function analysis, evaluation, creative, develop recommendations, presentation, and finally implementation and follow-up. Each phase has its own purpose, objectives, and tasks. For example, the creative phase involves exploring the various ways to perform the function(s) identified in the function analysis phase. This allows team members to brainstorm alternatives to existing systems or methods that are in use. Brainstorming forces people to be creative and allows team members to speculate on all possible ideas to the problems presented, or alternatives to the function. Figure 29-1: Proposed Value Engineering Process for DGII Infrastructure Project Jacobs ideal proposition for DGII is to conduct VE workshop soon after completion of 60% preliminary design and cost estimates. Subsequently, the outcome of the VE workshop shall be implemented during the execution of the 60% preliminary design stage. Soon after completion of this stage and cost estimates are adjusted accordingly, a second round of VE workshop was conducted on 6th April 2023 for gauging the previous implementation and identifying plausible areas that could possibly be fine-tuned and implemented during the execution of the 90% preliminary design and for generating new VE ideas. Based on final VE session, VE initiative has been included in the Package 1 detailed design. 29.2 Value Engineering Basics by validating functionality and providing an equal or better solution without compromising the efficacy of the service or product. At present, the Value Methodology Basics followed by Jacobs for DGII VE exercise is as per SAVE International VE process. Value is defined as the ratio of function to cost and thus value can be increased by either improving the function or by reducing the cost. Value = Function / Cost The value engineering should be initiated as early as possible in the project life cycle. If value engineering becomes rework or causes project delays, it is no longer beneficial to the project. The below graph shows when value engineering moves from presenting a financial gain to a financial loss. The lower down the project cycle we implement value engineering, it may become counterproductive to the overall project budget. STORM WATER NETWORK - GENERAL NOTES 1. ALL DIMENSIONS ARE IN METERS, UNLESS STATED OTHERWISE. 2. ALL LEVELS ARE IN METERS UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE. 3. THE SURVEY COORDINATE SYSTEM IS WGS84 - UTM 38 N AND LOCAL VERTICAL DATUM. 4. ALL DIMENSIONS SHALL BE VERIFIED ON SITE BEFORE PROCEEDING WITH THE WORK. 5. ALL DIMENSIONS SHOWN ON STANDARD DETAIL DRAWINGS ARE IN MILLIMETERS UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED. 6. THE CONTRACTOR HAS TO TAKE ALL NECESSARY PRECAUTIONS AND MEASURES TO DEAL WITH GROUNDWATER AND SURFACE WATER DURING CONSTRUCTION IN CASE WATER TABLE IS ENCOUNTERED. 7. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL VERIFY GROUND LEVELS BEFORE COMMENCEMENT OF WORK. 8. OIL INTERCEPTOR ARE PROPRIETARY ITEMS AND IT SHALL BE THE CONTRACTOR'S RESPONSIBILITY TO DESIGN AND CONSTRUCT AS PER MANUFACTURER'S STANDARDS AND RECOMMENDATIONS AND AS APPROVED BY THE EMPLOYER'S REPRESENTATIVE. 9. ANY DEVIATIONS FROM THE ALLOCATED CORRIDORS SHALL BE AGREED WITH THE EMPLOYER'S REPRESENTATIVE PRIOR TO CONSTRUCTION COMMENCEMENT. 10. COVER LEVEL OF MANHOLES/CHAMBERS SHOULD MATCH WITH SURROUNDING BITUMINOUS /PAVED AREAS. 11. ALL CONCRETE SHALL BE CLASS 'A' UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED. SULFATE RESISTING PORTLAND CEMENT (TYPE V) COMPLYING WITH BS 4027 SHALL BE USED IN ALL CONCRETE MIXES. 12. STEEL REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE GRADE 460 (BS 4449) STEEL BARS OR AS SPECIFIED. 13. ALL REINFORCEMENT IN MANHOLES/CHAMBERS SHALL BE EPOXY COATED AS SPECIFIED. 14. MINIMUM COVER TO REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE 50mm, UNLESS SPECIFIED OTHERWISE . 15. EXTERNAL CONCRETE SURFACES BELOW GROUND SHALL BE PROTECTED WITH BITUMINOUS WATERPROOF MEMBRANE 2.20mm AND PROTECTION BOARD 6.0mm AS SPECIFIED. 16. GRANOLITHIC CONCRETE SHALL BE FORMED IN ALL MANHOLE CHANNELS TO PROVIDE A SMOOTH TRANSITION OF SIZE AND GRADIENT FROM THE INLET(S) TO THE OUTLET STORM INVERTS. 17. ALL MANHOLES TO HAVE 3 COATS OF EPOXY PAINT PROTECTION LINING TO ALL EXPOSED INTERNAL CONCRETE SURFACES. 18. INTERNAL CEMENT MORTAR JOINTS OF STORM MANHOLE EXTENSION RINGS SHALL BE RAKED OUT AND ALL EXPOSED FACES SHALL BE LAMINATED WITH EPOXY PAINT. 19. ALL PIPES CONNECTED TO THE MANHOLES ARE TO BE PROVIDED WITH ADEQUATE PUDDLE FLANGES AS REQUIRED. 20. ALL STORM MANHOLES SHALL BE FITTED WITH HEAVY DUTY D400 DI COVERS TO BS EN 124. 21. GRANULAR BED AND SURROUND TO PIPES SHALL BE ENCLOSED IN GEOTEXTILE AS SPECIFIED FOR ALL PIPES. 22. ANY PIPELINE BELOW GROUND LEVEL ENTERING OR PROTRUDING FROM ANY STRUCTURE SHALL BE FITTED WITH TWO FLEXIBLE JOINTS ADJACENT TO THE STRUCTURE AS SPECIFIED UNLESS INDICATED OTHERWISE. 23. CONCRETE SURROUND SHALL BE PROVIDED TO STORMWATER PIPES WHERE THE COVER IS LESS THAN 1.2 METERS. 24. THE OIL INTERCEPTORS SHOWN IN THE DRAWINGS ARE OPTIONAL AND WILL BE USED IN CASE THERE IS NO OIL INTERCEPTOR LOCATED BEFORE THE POND IN THE WADI AREA. 25. INLET TYPE (EITHER CATCH BASIN OR KERB INLET) ARE INDICATIVE FOLLOWING THE DESIGN AND CORRIDORS. IN CASE CONTRACTOR FOUND ON SITE THAT TYPE OF INLET NEEDS TO BE CHANGED FOLLOWING THE ROAD AND SITE CONDITIONS , HE CAN PROCEED ACCORDINGLY. 26. HOUSE CONNECTIONS LOCATIONS ARE INDICATIVE AND TO BE CONFIRMED WITH PLOT OWNERS. 27. HOUSE CONNECTIONS OF PUMPSTATIONS TO BE CONNECTED TO THE OUTLET PIPES COMING FROM THE PUMP STATIONS

1. ALL PIPE DIAMETERS ARE IN MILLIMETER WHILE ALL OTHER DIMENSION ARE IN METER UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED. 2. PIPE DIAMETER LESS THAN 300MM ARE HDPE PIPES (PN16) WITH SDR -11 PE-100 AND DIAMETER EQUAL TO AND GREATER THAN Ø300 DUCTILE IRON PIPES CLASS C AND OPERATING PRESSURE 24 BAR SHALL BE USED FOR WHOLE POTABLE & FIRE WATER SYSTEM. 3. GATE VALVES SHALL BE DIRECT BURIED WITH SURFACE BOXES FOR PIPE DIA LESS THAN Ø300 WHILE FOR PIPE DIAMETER EQUAL TO AND LARGER THAN Ø300 SHOULD BE IN CONCRETE CHAMBERS. BUTTERFLY VALVES SHALL BE INSTALLED INSIDE CONCRETE CHAMBERS FOR PIPE DIA EQUAL TO AND MORE THAN Ø300. 4. POTABLE & FIRE WATER LINE SHALL BE INSTALLED WITH A SOIL COVER DEPTH OF 1.2M UNDER MAJOR ROADS AND 1.0M UNDER LOCAL ROADS. 5. A HORIZONTAL SEPARATION OF 3 METERS AND A VERTICAL SEPARATION OF 0.50 METER SHALL BE MAINTAINED BETWEEN POTABLE WATER AND SEWER LINES WITH THE SEWER LINE BELOW THE WATER LINE. A HORIZONTAL SEPARATION OF MINIMUM 3.00 METERS SHALL BE MAINTAINED WHERE A MINIMUM OF 0.50 METER VERTICAL SEPARATION CANNOT BE ACHIEVED. AT CROSS OVERS, WHERE THE VERTICAL SEPARATION CANNOT BE MAINTAINED WITH WATER LINE, THE SEWER LINE SHALL BE ENCASED IN CONCRETE FOR A MINIMUM LENGTH OF 3.00 METERS ON EACH SIDE OF THE WATER LINE. 6. CONCRETE THRUST BLOCKS SHALL BE PROVIDED AT ALL PIPE BENDS, TEES, REDUCERS AND INCASE OF CHANGE IN DIRECTION BOTH HORIZONTAL AND VERTICAL FOR DUCTILE IRON PIPES. FOR HDPE COMPLY WITH SUPPLIER RECOMMENDATIONS, THRUST BLOCK WILL NOT BE REQUIRED FOR HDPE PIPE IF FUSION WELDED. 7. PIPES HAVING COVER LESS THAN 1.0M SHALL BE ENCASED IN PLAIN CONCRETE. 8. ALL SERVICE CONNECTION PIPES SHALL BE INSTALLED AT DEPTH 0.80 TO 1.0 METER FROM FINISHED GRADE LEVEL. 9. FOR EXACT LOCATION OF POTABLE & FIRE WATER PIPE LINE REFER TO TYPICAL UTILITIES COORDINATION CROSS SECTIONS DRAWINGS. 10.AIR VALVES TO BE INSTALLED AT THE HIGHEST POINTS OF THE PIPES PROFILES. POTABLE WATER & FIRE FIGHTING NETWORK - GENERAL NOTES 11. FOR EXACT LOCATION OF FIRE HYDRANT TO BE COORDINATED WITH ENTRANCE (VILLA), TREES, OTHER STREET SPACE AND CIVIL DEFENCE. 12. FIRE HYDRANTS ARE PLACED AT INTERVAL OF 150M IN RESIDENTIAL AREA AND 90M IN COMMERCIAL AND HIGH-RISK AREAS AS PER NFPA / CIVIL DEFENCE/ MEWA GUIDELINES AND 75M IN ICONIC AREAS. 13. ALL PIPE DIAMETERS ARE NOMINAL PIPE SIZES,FOR HDPE, IT IS OUTSIDE AND FOR DUCTILE IRON IT IS INSIDE.. 14. CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE TO VERIFY THE GROUND LEVELS. THE TOP OF CHAMBERS SHALL BE FLUSH WITH THE ASPHALT PAVEMENT OR WITH FINISHED SIDEWALK LEVELS IN PAVED STREETS AND IN UNPAVED AREAS AS SOWN ON PLAN. 15. IN CASE OF ANY DAMAGE TO ANY PROPERTY OR UTILITY DURING CONSTRUCTION OF THIS PROJECT. CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE TO RE-CONSTRUCT AND RECOVER THE PROPERTY OR UTILITY TO ITS ORIGINAL FORM ON HIS OWN COST. 16. IN CASE OF ANY CLASHES BETWEEN UTILITIES, THE CONTRACTOR MUST ACHIEVE 500MM OF CLEARANCE ON THE VERTICAL POSITION OF THE UTILITIES.IN CREATING SEPARATION OF THE UTILITIES, WATER PIPE SHOULD BE ABOVE IRRIGATION PIPE.

THE DIAMETER AND MATERIAL SHALL BE CO-ORDINATED ACCURATELY WITH THE NETWORK OUTSIDE. 14. SUPPORT DETAILS FOR ALL EQUIPMENT INCLUDING PUMPS & VESSELS SHALL BE CONFIRMED BY THE CONTRACTOR/MANUFACTURER. 15. ADEQUATE SUPPORTS SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR ALL THE ABOVE GROUND PIPING. 16. PORTABLE LIFTING DAVIT SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR EACH LIFTING STATION WITH SOCKETS PROPOSED AT ALL LOCATIONS TO LIFT THE PUMPS AND VALVES. 20. IRRIGATION DISTRIBUTION AND PRIMARY NETWORK - GENERAL NOTES 1) ALL PIPE DIAMETERS ARE IN MILLIMETER WHILE ALL OTHER DIMENSION ARE IN METER UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED. 2) PIPE DIAMETER LESS THAN AND EQUAL TO 600MM ARE HDPE PIPES PN16 (SDR-11) AND PN20 (SDR-9) AND GREATER THAN 600MM GRP PIPES STIFFNESS SN10,000 N/m² (PN16 AND PN20) SHALL BE USED FOR WHOLE IRRIGATION SYSTEM. 3) GATE VALVES SHALL BE DIRECT BURIED WITH SURFACE BOXES FOR PIPE DIA LESS THAN Ø200 WHILE FOR PIPE DIAMETER EQUAL TO AND LARGER THAN Ø200 SHOULD BE IN CONCRETE CHAMBERS. BUTTERFLY VALVES SHALL BE INSTALLED INSIDE CONCRETE CHAMBERS FOR PIPE DIA EQUAL TO AND MORE THAN Ø300. 4) IRRIGATION LINE SHALL BE INSTALLED WITH A SOIL COVER DEPTH OF 1.2m UNDER MAJOR ROADS AND 1.0m UNDER LOCAL ROADS. 5) THRUST BLOCK FOR HDPE PIPE SHALL COMPLY WITH SUPPLIER RECOMMENDATIONS, THRUST BLOCK WILL NOT BE REQUIRED FOR HDPE PIPE IF FUSION WELDED. CONCRETE THRUST BLOCKS SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR ALL OTHER PIPES AT ALL PIPE BENDS, TEES, REDUCERS AND INCASE OF CHANGE IN DIRECTION BOTH HORIZONTAL AND VERTICAL FOR DUCTILE IRON PIPES. 6) PIPES HAVING COVER LESS THAN 1.0m SHALL BE ENCASED IN PLAIN CONCRETE. 7) PRESSURE CAN BE REDUCED TO DESIRED LEVEL USING PRV AT PLOT CONNECTION (MAXIMUM 5 BAR) AND AT SOLENOID VALVE(MAXIMUM 7BAR). ALL PRV INSTALLATION SHALL FOLLOW THE ARRANGEMENT AS SHOWN IN STANDARD DETAILS DRAWING. 8) FOR EXACT LOCATION OF IRRIGAITON PIPE LINE REFER TO TYPICAL UTILITIES COORDINATION CROSS SECTIONS DRAWINGS. 9) INSTALL AIR / VACUUM RELIEF VALVES AT IRRIGATION MAIN LINE TERMINATION POINTS, OR TO HIGHEST POINTS AND FINAL LOCATION TO BE ADJUSTED SITE. 10) ALL PIPE DIAMETERS ARE NOMINAL PIPE SIZES, FOR HDPE, IT IS OUTSIDE AND FOR GRP, IT IS INSIDE. 11) CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE THE LOCAL AUTHORITIES / MUNICIPALITIES TO OBTAIN THE CONSTRUCTION APPROVAL BEFORE CONSTRUCTION. 12) ALL EXISITNG UTILITIES SYSTEMS SHALL BE KEPT IN OPERATION UNTIL THE NEW SYSTEM IS PUT IN TO OPERATION, AND IN FULL COORDINAITON WITH CONCERNED AUTHORITIES. 13) THE IRRIGATION SYSTEM IS DISPLAYED DIAGRAMMATIC, AND THE CONTRACTOR MAY BE REQUIRED TO MAKE ADJUSTMENTS IN THE FIELD AT THE TIME OF INSTALLATION TO AVOID EXISTING OR PLANNED UTILITIES. THE CONTRACTOR, HOWEVER, IS ADVISED TO FOLLOW THE LAYOUT AS SHOWN ON THE PLAN AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE 14) INCASE OF CONFLICT OR DISCREPANCY BETWEEN THE INFORMATION SHOWN AND ACTUAL CONDITION ON SITE, CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE SHOP DRAWING AND SUBMIT TO THE ENGINEER FOR APPROVAL PRIOR TO COMMENCEMENT OF CONSTRUCTION. 15) FOR INTERFACE CONNECTION, CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE TO LOCATE THE EXISTING SOURCE (INTERFACE POINT) FOR THE PROJECT AREA AND MAKE CONNECTION WITH IRRIGATION MAIN SUPPLY SYSTEM. 16) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE WITH ALL RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITIES AND MINISTRIES REGARDING DATA OR LOCATION OF ALL EXISITNG UTILITIES AND REPORT TO THE ENGINEER. 17) THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DISCONNECTION AND RECONNECTION OF THE EXISTING SERVICES TO THE NETWORK. 18) CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE TO VARIFY THE GROUND LEVELS. THE TOP OF CHAMBERS SHALL BE FLUSH WITH THE ASPHALT PAVEMENTOR WITH FINISHED SIDEWALK LEVELS IN PAVED STREETS AND IN UNPAVED AREAS AS

# Scaffolds — Site Safety Criteria (OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart L) REAL, sourced scaffold thresholds for construction sites. Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.451 (Subpart L, general requirements), US federal regulation, public domain. US-reference standard: in Saudi Arabia site HSE is governed by Saudi labour law (MHRSD) and the project HSE plan, not OSHA, but Saudi practice broadly aligns. Use as an engineering reference; enforce against the project HSE plan and the scaffold manufacturer's / designer's data. Values are metric-led (SI) with the original US-customary figure in parentheses. ## Capacity and stability## Capacity and stability | Parameter | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Load capacity (support own weight plus intended load ×) | 4× intended load | 4× intended load | | Height-to-base-width ratio above which restraint (guy/tie/brace) is required | more than 4 : 1 | more than 4 : 1 |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.451(a)(1), (c)(1). ## Fall protection and guardrails## Fall protection and guardrails | Parameter | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Height above which fall protection is required on a scaffold | 3.05 m | 10 ft | | Guardrail top-rail height (platforms manufactured after 1 Jan 2000) | 0.97–1.15 m | 38–45 in | | Maximum gap between platform and uprights (normal) | 2.5 cm | 1 in | | Maximum gap between platform and uprights (where wider is required) | 24.1 cm | 9½ in |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.451(g)(1), (g)(4)(ii), (b)(1). ## Minimum clearance from energized power lines## Minimum clearance from energized power lines | Line voltage | Minimum clearance (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Insulated, under 300 V | 0.9 m | 3 ft | | Uninsulated / under 50 kV | 3.05 m | 10 ft | | Over 50 kV | 3.05 m + 10 mm per kV over 50 kV | 10 ft + 0.4 in per kV over 50 kV |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.451(f)(6). ## KSA applicability OSHA 1926 is a US-reference standard, not the governing authority in Saudi Arabia (site HSE is under Saudi labour law / MHRSD and the project HSE plan). Saudi practice broadly aligns on the 4× capacity factor, fall protection at ~3 m, and power-line clearances. Where a value is enforced on site, confirm it against the project HSE plan and the scaffold designer's data. ## How to use - Quote the SI value for site use; cite the US original and the regulation number so the basis is traceable. - The scaffold manufacturer's / designer's rated data and the project HSE plan take precedence over these reference figures. - State that this is a US-reference figure, not the governing authority for a Saudi project.

The infrastructure package is divided in 3 packages: Package I, Package II and Package III. The below scope of works covers Package I currently but will extend to Packages II and III as optional after agreement with the Client. The information for existing networks for dry and wet utilities has been obtained from the stakeholders/ service providers; however, the accuracy of the information needs to be validated to avoid unforeseen circumstances/ scenarios. This is also fundamental as utility service provisions to existing users will need to be maintained till specific and discrete dates. The existing service connections will be terminated in phases, as the areas become available. The survey should give DGCL a comprehensive picture on the existing utility infrastructure in the highlighted area(s) above which will allow them to identify and quantify to the highest degree of accuracy the amount of utility protection, demolition, diversion needed to carry out the proposed Master Plan in the said zone. It is to be noted that all the information provided as part of the scope of works is to be treated as ‘For Information Only’. Any text/notes on the drawing not relevant will be ignored. • HV Network (Appendix ‘A’) • MV Network (Appendix ‘B’) • LV Network (Appendix ‘C’) • Telecom Network including GCC Cable (Appendix ‘D’) • Potable Water Network (Appendix ‘E’) • Wastewater Network (Appendix ‘F’) In addition to the above, topographical survey of the area is also available, as ‘For Information Only’, which can be made available to the Contractor upon request. 3. Scope To provide a Complete Utility Identification Survey Report for DII Project Site, based on the following list of minimum works but not limited to: 1- Supervision of the works. Coordinate and conduct a comprehensive site visit for understanding the client’s requests and needs. The Contractor will ensure full compliance with Safety standards as per Contract. 3- As-Built records/drawings. # Fall Protection — Site Safety Criteria (OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart M) REAL, sourced fall-protection thresholds for construction sites. Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502 (Subpart M), US federal regulation, public domain. This is a US-reference standard: in Saudi Arabia site HSE is governed by Saudi labour law (MHRSD) and the project's approved HSE plan, not OSHA — but Saudi practice broadly aligns with these figures. Use as an engineering reference; enforce against the project HSE plan. Values are metric-led (SI) with the original US-customary figure, as written in the regulation, in parentheses. ## Guardrail systems## Guardrail systems | Parameter | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Top-rail height above walking surface | 1.1 m (± 8 cm) | 42 in (± 3 in) | | Top-rail minimum strength (force withstood) | 890 N | 200 lbf | | Maximum opening / midrail gap | 0.48 m | 19 in | | Toeboard minimum vertical height | 9 cm | 3½ in |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(b), (j). ## Personal fall arrest system (PFAS)## Personal fall arrest system (PFAS) | Parameter | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Maximum arresting force on the body (harness) | 8 kN | 1,800 lbf | | Maximum free-fall distance | 1.8 m | 6 ft | | Maximum deceleration distance | 1.07 m | 3½ ft | | Anchorage strength, per attached worker | 22.2 kN | 5,000 lbf |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(d). Note: anchorage may instead be part of a system designed and used under a qualified person's supervision at a safety factor of 2. ## Hole and opening covers Covers over holes must be capable of supporting at least twice the combined weight of workers, equipment, and materials that may be imposed on them (rated to 2x the imposed load), and must be secured and colour-coded or marked "HOLE" / "COVER". Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(i). ## KSA applicability: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502(i). ## KSA applicability OSHA 1926 is US federal site-safety law and is not the governing authority in Saudi Arabia. Site HSE in KSA is regulated under Saudi labour law (MHRSD) and the project's approved HSE/safety plan; SBC (Saudi Building Code) governs building design, not site safety. These thresholds are a US engineering reference. Saudi practice broadly aligns: guardrails ~1.0–1.1 m high, a1.8 m free-fall limit, andails ~1.0–1.1 m high, a1.8 m free-fall limit, and PFAS anchorage in the 22 kN range. Where a value is enforced on site, confirm it against the project HSE plan. ## How to use - Fall protection is generally required at a fall height of 1.8 m (6 ft) or more in construction (Subpart M general trigger, 1926.501). - Quote the SI value for site use; cite the US original and the regulation number so the basis is traceable. - State that this is a US-reference figure and that the project HSE plan / local regulation takes precedence where they differ. - Do not present OSHA as the legal authority for a Saudi project — it is a reference standard

Diriyah Gate II Development 48 4.5 Pre-Construction Survey Prior to the commencement of construction and demolition activities, a pre-construction survey must be undertaken to identify all environmental aspects such as the following (but not limited to): ▪ Air Quality: - Visual and PM10 monitoring at Project boundary points located near identified SRs; ▪ Noise and Vibration Levels: - Baseline conditions should be monitored one month before commencement of construction and demolition activities; ▪ Soil contamination. A visual or olfactory inspection should be undertaken for the following: - Inspection for any contamination and spillages; - Identification of land uses and activities with potential sources of contamination; - Discoloured soil and/or fibrous texture to the soil (e.g., asbestos). Odour can also indicate contamination with the release of noxious fumes; - Foreign objects present; - Previous soil workings; - Waste pits; ▪ Water and wastewater: - If dewatering is required, baseline groundwater monitoring (including groundwater levels and quality) shall be undertaken; ▪ Ecology: - A terrestrial ecology survey will be undertaken in the form of a site walkover around the Project area, work site areas, access roads and buildings; - Pre-construction monitoring should be undertaken to locate potential ecological assets that may require relocation / protection (e.g., native trees, lizard burrows, nesting birds and roosting bats); ▪ Archaeology / Cultural Heritage: - Surveys carried out by professional archaeologists; - Drone survey; - Demarcation of areas with potential archaeological significance; ▪ Traffic and Transport; - Baseline traffic and routes assessment is recommended for planning of routes; and, - Noise and vibration monitoring. Photographic evidence of baseline conditions shall form part of the pre-construction survey. 4.6 Environmental and Sustainability Monitoring and Reporting MOSTADAM for Communities and LEED for Cities are the preferred certification schemes to be pursued and will be adopted at various target levels and in various districts of DG II. for Detection and Verification of Existing Underground Utilities The Purpose of this is to detection and verification of the underground utilitiesprior to commencement of any excavation works to ensure safety of the project operatives, personnel and the public; to avoid damages to buried utilities and assets. The process described in this can be summarized in the following : : Desktop utility record search includes the process of deification of the existing utilities within the survey area or the scope of work limits through the collation and analysis of existing as-built records. This should be carried out through the following process: Identify utility owners within the limit of works or survey area using the following source of information: Utility as-built drawings provided by the Client, PMC or the Engineer. BALADY Coordination certificate obtained by the Contractor. Refer to Appendix-1 for a sample of the coordination certificate. Note: Potential utility owners include SEC, NWC, Traffic police, Riyadh Municipality, DGCL AMCO, SWC, MODA, STC, Mobily, MEWA, etc. Upon identification of the affected utility owners, the Contractor will approach the identified utility owners to solicit up-to-date information and as-built drawings regarding the existing utilities. Deliverable of this step: The Contractor should collate the obtained as-built information and produce combined utility as-built records. The mentioned records to be composed of colored utility lines imposed on aerial images. Utility lines should indicate (as applicable) utility owner, type of utility, size, and depth (e.g. NWC; PW line, DI 300 mm, 1.5 m depth). Above records should be reviewed and approved by the CSC. Site reconnaissance shall compromise of a joint site visit by the Contractor and the CSC to validate the existing utility records obtained from step-1 and document the following: The presence of utility related surface features including manholes, inspection chambers, utility markers, feeder pillars, street lighting, traces of excavated trenches on paved roads, etc. Measurements between known surface features on the ground compared with those indicated in the utility records. Assessment of any conflicts between obtained utility records and actual site conditions. Deliverables of this step should include mark-up of the utility records along with supporting photographs. Detection: Detection involves the use of geophysical techniques to detect and locate the underground utilities within the survey area. Two techniques are generally applied to locate buried utilities: EML, Electro Magnetic Locating: Detection of buried utilities via a hand-held receiver using electromagnetic and radio frequency signals that are present in metallic utilities because of current flow or re-transmitted low frequency radio signals. GPR, Ground Penetrating Radar: The use of radar waves from a surface transmitter that can penetrate through ground materials and are reflected back to the instrument by a change of ground materials or other buried objects. The process of scanning utilities shall be as outlined below: Scanning device: The Contractor shall Submit technical data sheet, user manual, and calibration certificate for the CSC review / information. The Contractor to provide details of the device operator. Evidence of training provided either by the device manufacturer or amanufacturers’ s endorsed trainer has to be submitted to the CSC. The CSC

# Crane Power-Line Clearance — Site Safety Criteria (OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart CC) REAL, sourced minimum approach distances between cranes and energized overhead power lines. Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1408 Table A (Subpart CC), US federal regulation, public domain. US-reference standard: in Saudi Arabia site HSE is governed by Saudi labour law (MHRSD), the project HSE plan, and the utility operator (SEC), not OSHA, but the clearance principle is universal. The reg states the distances in feet only; SI equivalents below are converted. Always confirm the actual required clearance with the line's utility owner/operator. ## Minimum clearance to energized overhead power lines (crane operation)## Minimum clearance to energized overhead power lines (crane operation) | Line voltage (nominal, phase-to-phase) | Minimum clearance (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Up to 50 kV | 3.05 m | 10 ft | | Over 50 to 200 kV | 4.6 m | 15 ft | | Over 200 to 350 kV | 6.1 m | 20 ft | | Over 350 to 500 kV | 7.62 m | 25 ft | | Over 500 to 750 kV | 10.67 m | 35 ft | | Over 750 to 1,000 kV | 13.72 m | 45 ft |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1408 Table A. For voltages over 1,000 kV, the minimum clearance must be established by the utility owner/operator or a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person for electrical transmission and distribution. ## KSA applicability OSHA 1926 is a US-reference standard, not the governing authority in Saudi Arabia. On a KSA site the required clearance is set by the project HSE plan andired clearance is set by the project HSE plan and the utility owner/operator (typically the Saudi Electricity Company). Treat the table as a reference minimum; the utility's stated distance governs. ## How to use - Quote the SI value for site use; cite the US original and the regulation so the basis is traceable. - Before any crane work near power lines, confirm the actual required clearance with the utility owner/operator (SEC in KSA) — their distance takes precedence. - Where the line cannot be de-energized or cleared, a dedicated spotter, range-limiting device, or line-relocation may be required per the HSE plan.

Dubai Building Code 2021 Edition Dubai Building Code Contents ii Part A Part F Part G Part H Part K Part B Part C Part E Part D General Structure Architecture Incoming utilities Accessibility Indoor environment Vertical transportation Part J Security Building envelope Villas Dubai Building Code Part A General A 1 A.1 Introduction A.2 Definitions A.3 References A.4 Relationship of DBC to other local and international regulations A.5 Scope and application of the DBC A.6 Navigating the DBC A.7 Adoption of DBC A.8 Alternative solutions A.9 Maintenance of DBC A.10 Copyright A.11 Coordinate system A.12 Dimensions, units and calculations Dubai Building Code Part A: General A 2 A.1 Introduction The objective of the Dubai Building Code (DBC) is to unify building design across Dubai, and to create a building code that is easy to use and clearly mandates the minimum requirements for: a) the health, safety, welfare and convenience of people in and around buildings; b) the health, safety, welfare and convenience of people who might be affected by buildings; c) building design to reduce the impact on the surrounding environment; and d) the sustainable development of buildings. The content of the DBC is based on the following inputs: 1) existing regulations and technical requirements produced by the various Authorities and Service Providers; 2) interviews with Government Authorities, Service Providers, Master Developers, Consultants and other stakeholders to understand gaps or inconsistencies between existing regulations; 3) benchmarking to international and regional codes. The DBC is arranged under themes to integrate all relevant elements of building design. The regulations stipulated in the DBC are the minimum requirements for building design. Nothing in the DBC prevents a building design that achieves higher standards than the minimum set out in the DBC. Document history and status Distribution of copies Executive summary The attached details a number of obstacles following the planned clearance of the SEC site by the end of July 2025. The most concern lies in the connection of utilities which has not been factored into the SEC planned clearance pre-dominantly the reservoir overflow tank which cannot be moved and impedes the storm water connection as per below. The NGL (Natural Ground Level) has been built up with unscreened fill which need to removed to a Municipality dump as part of the works together with a number of other obstacles outlined within this report. Introduction The Contractor has been instructed by the Client to carry out the Gateway-1 Infrastructure work. Gateway-1 is located at the northern side of the Northern Ring Road as indicated in the below pictures. The Scope of the work related to the Infra-1 contractor is indicated in the below snip The area was previously occupied by Saudi Electric Company (SEC) as a laydown area for the construction of the HV substations and network. Following the instruction to AICC to carry out the infrastructure work at Gatweway-1, a site visit was carried out to assess the existing conditions of the site and to enable the site handover from SEC to Infra-1. Site Obstacles Several obstacles within the Right-of-Way (ROW) of the infra-1 have been identified as indicated in the below snip. The details of the above-mentioned obstacles are listed in the below table: Site Topography The site topography has been artificially raised by approximately 1 to 4 meters using unconsolidated fill materials and construction debris (refer to the images below). These materials must be excavated and removed to restore the site to its original natural ground level (NGL) before commencing earthwork activities. At present, the exact volume of these materials cannot be accurately determined due to the lack of historical elevation data. However, a preliminary estimate suggests that the volume of unconsolidated material is approximately 30,000 cubic meters. Detailed Design Report_extract Package 1 - IP-INF-054-0000-JCB-RPT-DE-000013 [A] 24 January 2024 Potable Water and Firefighting (page 154 and next) “It shall be noted that the potable water alignment and design was based on the Masterplan of DGII 14.1.5 Rev08, further changes in the masterplan shall be considered in the upcoming submissions.” Introduction The concept of potable water system is to take main supply from National Water Company (NWC) water line 1200 mm (JF: or 1000mm as mention ahead?) located in King Khalid Road (KKR) (under construction) (JF: details of this project? Work programme coordinated with ours?) to supply the three proposed tanks in the development. Connection points: 2 in the north side of the development feeding Tank-1 and Tank-2 and 1 in the south side of KKR feeding Tank-3. The distribution system should include water connection to each building unit up to its boundary plot maintaining minimum pressure requirement as per NWC/MEWA standards. Individual plots developers shall be responsible for the design and construction of their internal potable water distribution systems. (Easting and Northing) shall be confirmed with NWC & DGCL. Design objectives and constraints Main objective of the hydraulic design is to achieve a minimum pressure requirement of 1.5 bar at all locations. The information about existing pressure at the source point in NWC network on the KKR road is not available yet, The design will be amended in the later stage’s once information about pressure at tie-in point and location is confirmed by the authority (JF: this is a major constrain and may lead to time and/or cost impact) Existing Potable Water Network The (existing) network is seen to be located along King Khalid Road (KKR), within Districts DE3, 5, 7, 8, and 11. Pipe diameters are varying in size from 110 mm to 1200 mm. Pipe material for the combined potable water/firefighting systems includes uPVC, Cast Iron (CI), Ductile Iron (DI) and Asbestos Cement (AC), Concrete Cylindrical Pipe (CCP). All existing AC pipes within the project boundary will have to be replaced and adequality removed according to health organizations standards. These include the 300 mm and 600 mm diameter pipelines along King Khalid Road. Discussion and coordination with NWC on these alternatives shall take place. (JF: work by which project? Infra? Demolitions?. Coordination required between AIC and third party/stakeholder) Design Basis and Criteria Three storage reservoirs will be provided with total storage as one-day average demand plus fire water requirement (893 m3 in each tank (31 L/S for 4 Hours at two Hydrants), as a minimum level of redundancy. The pumps design shall follow the Peak daily Demand plus Fire Fighting demand (PDD + FF) and to assure minimum pressure in the network at the plot connection = 1.5 bar and maximum pressure up to 5.0 bar. House connection Type: As per NWC standards, a water connection will be composed of a saddle connection mounted on a waterline, connection pipes, water meter boxes and other related and necessary items to complete the house connection assembly…. size shallaccommodate filling the plot storage tank in 8 hours as per the NFPA

Part 1. FIDIC Conditions of Contract (Red Book) 1. 도급 계약 관련 Sample Letter 로서 총 100개의 Sample로 구성됨. 2. Sample Letters는 FIDIC Red book 기준으로 (1999년 Construction Only) 작성 되었음. 3. FIDIC 계약이라 하더라도, Design Build 또는 Turnkey 계약의 경우 일부 차이가 있을 수 있으므로 사용시 주의 필요함.[source: G:\My Drive\200-Project Controls Procedures\Templates & Others\TEM-211_150914_Legal Sample Letters Ver 1.0.docx] 또는 Turnkey 계약의 경우 일부 차이가 있을 수 있으므로 사용시 주의 필요함. Part 2. Samsung Standard Subcontract (Re-measurement) 1. 하도급 계약 관련 Sample Letter 로서 총 64개의 Sample로 구성됨. 2. 2015년 7월 27일 최종 개정된 당사 표준 하도급 계약서 (Re-measurement)를 기반으로 하여 작성 되었음. 3. Lump Sum 방식 및 Short Form 등의 일부 변경된 당사 표준 하도급 계약의 사용시 일부 차이가 있을 수 있으므로 주의 필요함. Part 3. Samsung Standard Purchase Order (Bulk Material – Fixed Rate) 1. 조달 계약 관련 Sample Letter 로서 총 30개의 Sample로 구성됨.[source: G:\My Drive\200-Project Controls Procedures\Templates & Others\TEM-211_150914_Legal Sample Letters Ver 1.0.docx] 1. 조달 계약 관련 Sample Letter 로서 총 30개의 Sample로 구성됨. 2. 2015년 1월 12일 최종 개정된 당사 표준 조달 계약서 (Bulk Material – Fixed Rate)를 기반으로 하여 작성 되었음. 3. 주기기 구입 및 일회성 구입 등의 일부 변경된 당사 표준 조달 계약의 사용시 일부 차이가 있을 수 있으므로 주의 필요함. Statement of Problem Urban infrastructures are becoming more complex last century. The importance of pipe detecting and the value of its application. Before excavation for maintenance of underground piping, it is necessary to understand the various site problems on topography and surface materials (e.g. position (depth and displacement) and size of other piping, as well as manholes); In order to prevent third party companies from possible damages to infrastructural equipments and people, severe damage will be generated from mistaken excavation of other piping. The severity might even affect the corporate image and living resources such as electricity, telecommunication and hydrology. Detection of underground pipeline and cable locations is very important, in addition, locations and positions of infrastructural elements with respect to each other must be known for the new infrastructural projects and for the process of operation and replacement of current infrastructure. 1.1. Introduction Developing Technologies are rapidly, so there are a lot of devices for the detection of pipeline and cable locations. These devices are working with two methods in general. One of them is electromagnetic detection method with electromagnetic induction, and the other is GPR (Ground Penetrating Radar) method working with the principle of determining the underground structure and underground holes. Especially with the new instruments and computer algorithms developed in the last years, the locations of infrastructural elements with respect to each other are determined more accurately. Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a geophysical method that uses radar pulses to image the subsurface. This non-destructive method uses electromagnetic (EM) radiation in the microwave band (UHF/VHF frequencies) of the radio spectrum, and detects the reflected signals from subsurface structures. One of the most useful applications of GPR in urban infrastructural engineering is mapping and detection of buried pipes. This unique application becomes imperative due to the ever-growing urbanization in both developed and developing nations with its attendant demand for buried utilities. The construction, development and management of subsurface infrastructures has become a very viable business that attracts the attention of scientists and engineers over the past few years. Various utilities such as telecommunication and electric power cables, water and gas supply cables etc. are delivered through underground pipes of various sized buried at different depths. In many cases, maintenance of these infrastructures requires digging operation which leads to unintentional damage to some of the facilities. Document history and status Distribution of copies Executive summary The attached details a number of obstacles following the planned clearance of the SEC site by the end of July 2025. The most concern lies in the connection of utilities which has not been factored into the SEC planned clearance pre-dominantly the reservoir overflow tank which cannot be moved and impedes the storm water connection as per below. The NGL (Natural Ground Level) has been built up with unscreened fill which need to removed to a Municipality dump as part of the works together with a number of other obstacles outlined within this report. Introduction The Contractor has been instructed by the Client to carry out the Gateway-1 Infrastructure work. Gateway-1 is located at the northern side of the Northern Ring Road as indicated in the below pictures. The Scope of the work related to the Infra-1 contractor is indicated in the below snip The area was previously occupied by Saudi Electric Company (SEC) as a laydown area for the construction of the HV substations and network. Following the instruction to AICC to carry out the infrastructure work at Gatweway-1, a site visit was carried out to assess the existing conditions of the site and to enable the site handover from SEC to Infra-1. Site Obstacles Several obstacles within the Right-of-Way (ROW) of the infra-1 have been identified as indicated in the below snip. The details of the above-mentioned obstacles are listed in the below table: Site Topography The site topography has been artificially raised by approximately 1 to 4 meters using unconsolidated fill materials and construction debris (refer to the images below). These materials must be excavated and removed to restore the site to its original natural ground level (NGL) before commencing earthwork activities. At present, the exact volume of these materials cannot be accurately determined due to the lack of historical elevation data. However, a preliminary estimate suggests that the volume of unconsolidated material is approximately 30,000 cubic meters. Obstruction Removal Cost Estimate The below table shows the breakdown of the cost estimate of the removal of the obstructions. ALJAZZAR g) ip ot I MOHAMMED OMAR JAZZAR CONSULTING ENGINEERS CO Auwsigl GILaiuS Ne ae dane AS yc 1. Statement of Problem Urban infrastructures are becoming more complex last century. The importance of pipe detecting and the value of its application. Before excavation for maintenance of underground piping, it is necessary to understand the various site problems on topography and surface materials (e.g. position (depth and displacement) and size of other piping, as well as manholes); In order to prevent third party companies from possible damages to infrastructural equipments and people, severe damage will be generated from mistaken excavation of other piping. The severity might even affect the corporate image and living resources such as electricity, telecommunication and hydrology. Detection of underground pipeline and cable locations is very important, in addition, locations and positions of infrastructural elements with respect to each other must be known for the new infrastructural projects and for the process of operation and replacement of current infrastructure. 1.1. Introduction Developing Technologies are rapidly, so there are a lot of devices for the detection of pipeline and cable locations. These devices are working with two methods in general. One of them is electromagnetic detection method with electromagnetic induction, and the other is GPR (Ground Penetrating Radar) method working with the principle of determining the underground structure and underground holes. Especially with the new instruments and computer algorithms developed in the last years, the locations of infrastructural elements with respect to each other are determined more accurately. Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a geophysical method that uses radar pulses to image the subsurface. This non-destructive method uses electromagnetic (EM) radiation in the microwave band (UHF/VHF frequencies) of the radio spectrum, and detects the reflected signals from subsurface structures. One of the most useful applications of GPR in urban infrastructural engineering is mapping and detection of buried pipes. This unique application becomes imperative due to the ever-growing urbanization in both developed and developing nations with its attendant demand for buried utilities. The construction, development and management of subsurface infrastructures has become a very viable business that attracts the attention of scientists and engineers over the past few years. Various utilities such as telecommunication and electric power cables, water and gas supply cables etc. are delivered through underground pipes of various sized buried at different depths. In many cases, maintenance of these infrastructures requires digging operation which leads to unintentional damage to some of the facilities. MoM Ref: [XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX] Revision: 00 Date: 6th Feb, 2025 Page: Page 1 of 2 Minutes of Meeting Portfolio DG2-Diriyah Gate II Project DD-2023-118 Infrastructure Package 1 Title Boulevard Conditional IFC DWGs Technical issues Workshop Meeting with DCo / AECOM/JACOBS and AL-AYUNI Date 6 Feb, 2025 Time: 09:11 Workshop Meeting Location: Microsoft Teams/ AICC Meeting Room Invite /Attendees Name Organization Designation Clive Walsh DC Infrastructure Associate Director Mohammad Jamal Khan DC Associate director Mohammad Mustafa AECOM Electrical Engineer Faiz Rasoul -FR (online) JACOBS Design Manager Ahmad Souliman JACOBS Wet utilities Engineer Magesh Mohan JACOBS Resident Engineer Ali Tipu JACOBS Construction Manager Akash Dhar JACOBS Structure Engineer Abdullah Sabri AICC Construction Director Mostafa Abdelwahab AICC Technical Manager Badraldin Adam AICC BIM Manager Yahya Samara AICC Lead Electrical Prepared By: Mohammad Mustafa Item Description Action Owner Due Date Status The Workshop aimed to discuss below raised technical issues by the contractor from the recent issued boulevard conditional IFC DWGs. Info 1 Storm Water Network: 1.1 AICC stated that the received SW conditional IFC DWG showing kerb inlet in the place of the catch basin, without any details for the kerb inlet, noting that the Kerb inlet will clash with the storm water line as there are not enough space in between. JACOBS stated that the kerb inlet is required by the client, and the typical details will be issued on Sunday 9th Feb 2025. 1.2 AICC expressed concern that the drawing indicates kerb inlets at both the beginning and end of the bus stop area, which could lead to water accumulation in the bus stop area. Jacobs is responsible for ensuring that the power estimation aligns with the detailed design report / PRS and dataset. This includes verifying the accuracy of the power estimation against the Plot Area, Gross Floor Area (GFA), land use levels, and other relevant parameters to ensure comprehensive and accurate power estimation. The following examples demonstrate some discrepancies between the Detailed Master Plan (DMP) / PRS and the power estimation report: The GFA of plot # DE6-MUO-RC-05, as per the detailed master plan / dataset, is recorded as 13474 m². However, the estimation power report lists it as 5974.19 m², indicating a discrepancy that needs addressing, which could affect the accuracy of power needs. This comment has been partially updated. Plot # DE6-MUO-RC-06A which are included in the power estimation report, are not recognized as part of District 6. Furthermore, this plot is not depicted in the Detailed Master Plan DMP / PRS and dataset. The GFA split for plot # DE6-MUO-RC-05, as indicated in the detailed master plan/dataset, varies from the power estimation. Jacobs must ensure that power load calculations are included for each plot and loop in the power estimation report. For instance, the current power estimation report does not account for the load calculations of plots DE1-RO-01, DE3-PM-04, and DE3-PM-05. This comment has been partially updated. For instance, the load estimation for plot DE8-PU-09 is missing from the power estimation report. The maximum load for each MV loop / cable as per SEC, as specified in the latest version of the Detailed Design Report, shall not exceed 6.46MVA. As mentioned in the DMP DGCL will load the MV loops up to 75-85% (of the 7.6MVA) of this derated SEC capacity to maintain enough spare in the cable for any unforeseen future load increase. However, it has been observed that for loop 11, the total load is currently at 7.5MVA, which exceeds the recommended maximum. Please provide a detailed justification for this discrepancy. We recommend Jacobs to adhere to SEC standards and project requirements regarding the maximum load of MV loops, ensuring that the load does not exceed the recommended limit of 6.42 MVA. Some loops currently exceed this recommendation. Jacobs is requested to provide detailed justifications for including a 10% contingency load in the power estimation report. The justification should explain why this contingency is necessary when the size and capacity of the MV (Medium Voltage) network and distribution substations are based on the total load, which includes the Final CDL + EV Chargers + Events, rather than the Plot CDL, which includes the contingency load. For instance, the load for loop #118 is calculated at 6,831.74 KVA, and MV SWGR-59 is rated at 6.83 MVA, aligning with the total load but excluding the contingency load (without accounting for the contingency load). Please explain the rationale behind this approach. This comment has been updated. # Interior Finishes Take-off and Estimate — the Process Contract How interior quantities and resource costs are derived on this platform. This document states the PROCESS. It deliberately contains **no heights, no productivity figures, no rates**: those are project variables that change per project and even per floor, and they must come from the project's own documents, the project facts store, or the operator — never from a global default. ## The processr — never from a global default. ## The process 1. **Measure** — the drawing take-off gives, per floor: net room floor area, summed room perimeter, and room count (`drawing_qto`). 2. **Derive interior quantities** — `interior_finishes_takeoff` computes: - floor screed / floor tiling / ceiling finish areas = net floor area; - skirting length = perimeter − (doors × door width); - wall finish area = perimeter × floor-to-ceiling height − door area − window deductions;ling height − door area − window deductions; - blockwork element area = wall face area × shared-wall fraction (internal walls are shared between two rooms; the fraction is a declared modelling parameter). The calculator REFUSES when the height is missing — it names the variable to supply instead of assuming one. 3. **Split resources** — `resource_line_cost` computes, per line: labour = quantity ÷ daily output × trade day rate; plant = declared÷ daily output × trade day rate; plant = declared fraction of labour; material = quantity × material rate. Productivity and day rate are required inputs; a missing material rate is reported as NO SOURCED RATE, never as zero and never invented. 4. **Source the variables, per project** — in this order: - the project's own documents (sections and door schedules for heights and openings; priced bills for rates);ights and openings; priced bills for rates); - the project facts / memory store (values the operator confirmed for THIS project — heights per floor, agreed norms, market rates); - the curated knowledge base's published references (composite rates, trade day rates, material prices) — cited by source; - the operator, asked directly, when none of the above carries the value. 5. **Declare** — every deliverable restates the variables used and theirdeliverable restates the variables used and their source. An estimate whose basis section cannot name where each variable came from is not finished. ## Why no defaults A default height or norm silently wrong for one floor poisons every quantity derived from it, and the error is invisible because nothing asked for the value. A refusal that names the missing variable costs one question; a wrong hardwired fact costs a re-measure. The calculators therefore fail loudly on missing required variables, and agents ask.

THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE TO VERIFY THE GROUND LEVELS. FOR CHAMBER/MANHOLE INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL WALLS PROTECTION REFER TO SPECIFICATION. 5. LOCATION OF MANHOLES, CHAMBERS AND ANCILLARY WORKS ARE INDICATIVE ONLY. EXACT LOCATION TO BE DETERMINED ON SITE BY THE CONTRACTOR IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE RELEVANT SERVICE AUTHORITY. 6. FOR PIPELINE BEDDING, MANHOLE/CHAMBER, DISCHARGE CHAMBER DETAILS REFER TO RELEVANT STANDARD INSTALLATION DRAWINGS. 7. SEWERAGE GRAVITY NETWORK PIPES ARE TO BE GLASS REINFORCED PLASTIC (GRP) FOR ALL PIPE SIZES UNLESS OTHERWISE STATED FROM NWC O&M DEPARTMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH SPECIFICATIONS. 8. UNLESS INDICATED OTHERWISE SEWAGE RISING MAIN PIPES ARE TO BE DUCTILE IRON (DI). ALL IN ACCORDANCE WITH SPECIFICATIONS. 9. CONCRETE PROTECTION TO BE PROVIDED FOR PIPES HAVING COVER OF LESS THAN 1.50M 10. PROVIDE TWO FLEXIBLE JOINTS TO VALVE CHAMBERS/MANHOLES. PLACE FIRST JOINT AT A DISTANCE NOT MORE THAN ONE DIAMETER. PLACE THE SECOND JOINT AT A DISTANCE (X) NOT MORE THAN THE FOLLOWING. - FOR D < 450 MM, X = 2 PIPE DIAMTERES. - FOR D <450 <1000 MM, X = 1.20 M - FOR D > 1000 MM, X = 1.8M 11. COVERS OF MANHOLES AND CHAMBERS SHALL BE INSCRIBED WITH TYPE OF UTILITY, AUTHORITY HAVING JURISDICTION AND GRADE OF COVER IN BOTHE ENGLISH AND ARABIC. 12. DEPTH OF MANHOLES SHOWN IN BOQ SHALL BE MEASURED AS PER SPECIFICATIONS AND STANDARD METHOD OF MEASUREMENT OF MOWE. 13. BENCHING SLOPE IN MANHOLES SHOULD NOT EXCEED 10%. 14. USE CIRCULAR FRAME WITH ALL CHAMBERS/MANHOLES COVERS. 15. ALL CHAMBER/MANHOLE COVER SHALL BE HEAVY DUTY SUITABLE FOR HEAVY VEHICULAR TRAFFIC. 16. BACKDROP TO BE PROVIDED IF LEVEL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN INCOMING PIPE AND MANHOLE INVERT LEVEL IS MORE THAN 60CM (H > 60 CM) 17. MINIMUM OF 30CM CLEARANCE TO BE KEPT BETWEEN SEWER PIPE AND EXISTING OR FUTURE PLANNED SERVICES. 18. THE CONTRACTOR IS TO CO-ORDINATE WITH OTHER SERVICE LAYOUTS AND SUBMIT SHOP DRAWINGS INDICATING PIPE SIZES, LEVELS, GRADES AND PROFILES. 19. MINIMAL DEPTH OF THE INSPECTION CHAMBER TO BE 0.9M AS MEASURED FROM GROUND SURFACE TO THE INSPECTION CHAMBER INVERT. 20. HOUSE CONNECTION PIPE DIAMETER FOR PLOTS TO BE MINIMUM 150 MM INTERNAL OR MIN 160 MM OUTSIDE DIAMETER. 21. FOR DISCREPANCIES OR OMISSIONS IN THIS DRAWING CONTACT THE ENGINEER PRIOR TO CONSTRUCTION. 22. THE COPYRIGHT OF THIS DRAWING IS VESTED IN THE ENGINEER AND MUST NOT BE COPIED OR REPRODUCED WITHOUT WRITTEN CONSENT. 23. WHERE A MANHOLE IS SHOWN AT THE ROAD/KERB INTERFACE, THE MANHOLE COVER SHALL BE LOCATED SUCH THAT IT IS PLACED EITHER AT THE ROAD OR ON THE VERGE AND NOT TO BE LOCATED ACROSS THE INTERFACE. 24. IF THE CONTRACTOR EXPERIENCES DIFFICULTY IN LOCATING THE SERVICES, HE SHALL CONTACT THE RELEVANT SERVICE AUTHORITY FORASSISTANCE. Information Classification: Public DGII UTILITY IDENTIFICATION SURVEY SCOPE OF WORKS DII UTILITY IDENTIFICATION SURVEY – Scope of Works AECOM Page 2 of 19 Information Classification: Public 1. Overview This document describes the Utility Identification Survey scope of works to be conducted in DII (Area shown in schematic below). The infrastructure package is divided in 3 packages: Package I, Package II and Package III. The below scope of works covers Package I currently but will extend to Packages II and III as optional after agreement with the Client. The information for existing networks for dry and wet utilities has been obtained from the stakeholders/ service providers; however, the accuracy of the information needs to be validated to avoid unforeseen circumstances/ scenarios. This is also fundamental as utility service provisions to existing users will need to be maintained till specific and discrete dates. The existing service connections will be terminated in phases, as the areas become available. The survey should give DGCL a comprehensive picture on the existing utility infrastructure in the highlighted area(s) above which will allow them to identify and quantify to the highest degree of accuracy the amount of utility protection, demolition, diversion needed to carry out the proposed Master Plan in the said zone. DII UTILITY IDENTIFICATION SURVEY – Scope of Works AECOM Page 3 of 19 Information Classification: Public 2. Existing Information The available information for the existing utilities with the Client is included herewith and covers the below. It is to be noted that all the information provided as part of the scope of works is to be treated as ‘For Information Only’. Any text/notes on the drawing not relevant will be ignored. • HV Network (Appendix ‘A’) • MV Network (Appendix ‘B’) • LV Network (Appendix ‘C’) • Telecom Network including GCC Cable (Appendix ‘D’) • Potable Water Network (Appendix ‘E’) • Wastewater Network (Appendix ‘F’) In addition to the above, topographical survey of the area is also available, as ‘For Information Only’, which can be made available to the Contractor upon request. 3. Scope To provide a Complete Utility Identification Survey Report for DII Project Site, based on the following list of minimum works but not limited to: 1- Supervision of the works. The Contractor must ensure to liaise with the Construction Supervision supervising its works to ensure that all procedures are stablished in advance of starting the works. 2- Site Visits. Coordinate and conduct a comprehensive site visit for understanding the client’s requests and needs. The Contractor will ensure full compliance with Safety standards as per Contract. 3- As-Built records/drawings. Before starting works on site, the contractor will endeavour all efforts to secure as much information (as-built records and drawings/ any other relevant information) as possible about all relevant buried and above ground assets to be surveyed, by establishing contact with Authorities and Service Providers and report on its findings accordingly. 4- Pre-condition photographic survey. Case Report Review of AMCO (Asset Management Company) Interfaces with Infrastructure team and Inherent delays Role Stakeholder Authority within Diriyah with specific oversight on Asset Management AMCO specifically reviewing all elements of the project that will be managed by them following Handover. Traffic Management Traffic Lighting Streetlighting ICT / Security Structure Breakdown in Terms of Infra Package 1 – AMCO Review Team Pedestrian underpasses – shared with AMCO on 15th Jan 2025 Traffic Management – Shared with AMCO on 21st Feb 2025 ICT/Security – shared with AMCO on 6th Feb 2025 Drafted By Clive Walsh Assoc Project Director 26th March 2025 Package Submission Review Package 1 Submission Description Underpass Structure (BVD and UPASS 2) Submission Date 15.01.25 Issue Type E-mail Days Overdue (allowing 14 days) 60 days Package 2 Submission Description Traffic Management Submission Date 21.02.25 Days Overdue (allowing 14 days) 19 days Package 3 Submission Description ICT/Security Submission Date 06.02.25 Days Overdue (allowing 14 days) 34 days Current Permit Flow Assessment Marked Red below – Areas where the PMC Stakeholder management team should be monitoring and requesting escalation but not happening Permit Flow-Diagram Review Key Observations and Findings AMCO have raised queries on the packages which have not been effectively communicated. This needs more investigation noting comments from Traffic Management package were received on 6th February 2025 and returned on 18th March 2025 (32 days to respond from DC team) and there is no other evidence of comments issued on the other packages. We note in addition that there is no set defined ruling for receipt of submissions with some using ACX ie. ICT and others standard mail with external zip files. (Appendix 1.0) AMCO requested a form to be completed referencing “AM Purpose of Request” The form returned was– noting Land Handover form issued and email (Appendix 2) – noting this is the request form but really does not suit the purpose of what’s required 3.0 No direct authorized person from Infrastructure DG2 Package 1 team following up is evident due to the passage of time without any visibility. Nobody owns the issue. Falling between two stools ; Nawar and Joao both poorly failing to address the key issues and no record of sufficient escalation controls evident. 4.0 Unclear Submissions referencing correspondence below leads to delays in Package Understanding Lots of examples of unclear direction and confusion on both sides of the Issuing and Receiving scale. Clear Roles and Responsibilities needed on both sides. 5.0 Consistent and Poor reporting by PMC Stakeholder management team. Noticing there is only a reporting functionality with Engr Anas (AECOM) with the weekly stakeholder meeting and reporting but no visible escalation and monitoring of consistent delays. This could be very well as a result of continuous delays in absolutely everything and now the team is tired to expedite anything and changes are recommended. 6.0 On both visits to AMCO on 25th and 26th March we found both key persons references marked “*” were working from home and unavailable. Rayan Bakhit Commercial Asst Manager*Abdul Rouf Bandith Assoc Design Direction *Abdul Haman Al Amri Design Director 7.0

STORM WATER NETWORK - GENERAL NOTES 1. ALL DIMENSIONS ARE IN METERS, UNLESS STATED OTHERWISE. 2. ALL LEVELS ARE IN METERS UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE. 3. THE SURVEY COORDINATE SYSTEM IS WGS84 - UTM 38 N AND LOCAL VERTICAL DATUM. 4. ALL DIMENSIONS SHALL BE VERIFIED ON SITE BEFORE PROCEEDING WITH THE WORK. 5. ALL DIMENSIONS SHOWN ON STANDARD DETAIL DRAWINGS ARE IN MILLIMETERS UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED. 6. THE CONTRACTOR HAS TO TAKE ALL NECESSARY PRECAUTIONS AND MEASURES TO DEAL WITH GROUNDWATER AND SURFACE WATER DURING CONSTRUCTION IN CASE WATER TABLE IS ENCOUNTERED. 7. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL VERIFY GROUND LEVELS BEFORE COMMENCEMENT OF WORK. 8. VORTEX MANHOLES AND OIL INTERCEPTORS ARE PROPRIETARY ITEMS AND IT SHALL BE THE CONTRACTOR'S RESPONSIBILITY TO DESIGN AND CONSTRUCT AS PER MANUFACTURER'S STANDARDS AND RECOMMENDATIONS AND AS APPROVED BY THE EMPLOYER'S REPRESENTATIVE. 9. ANY DEVIATIONS FROM THE ALLOCATED CORRIDORS SHALL BE AGREED WITH THE EMPLOYER'S REPRESENTATIVE PRIOR TO CONSTRUCTION COMMENCEMENT. 10. COVER LEVEL OF MANHOLES/CHAMBERS SHOULD MATCH WITH SURROUNDING BITUMINOUS /PAVED AREAS. 11. ALL CONCRETE SHALL BE CLASS 'A' UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED. SULFATE RESISTING PORTLAND CEMENT (TYPE V) COMPLYING WITH BS 4027 SHALL BE USED IN ALL CONCRETE MIXES. 12. STEEL REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE GRADE 460 (BS 4449) STEEL BARS OR AS SPECIFIED. 13. ALL REINFORCEMENT IN MANHOLES/CHAMBERS SHALL BE EPOXY COATED AS SPECIFIED. 14. MINIMUM COVER TO REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE 50mm, UNLESS SPECIFIED OTHERWISE . 15. EXTERNAL CONCRETE SURFACES BELOW GROUND SHALL BE PROTECTED WITH BITUMINOUS WATERPROOF MEMBRANE 2.20mm AND PROTECTION BOARD 6.0mm AS SPECIFIED. 16. GRANOLITHIC CONCRETE SHALL BE FORMED IN ALL MANHOLE CHANNELS TO PROVIDE A SMOOTH TRANSITION OF SIZE AND GRADIENT FROM THE INLET(S) TO THE OUTLET STORM INVERTS. 17. ALL MANHOLES TO HAVE 3 COATS OF EPOXY PAINT PROTECTION LINING TO ALL EXPOSED INTERNAL CONCRETE SURFACES. 18. INTERNAL CEMENT MORTAR JOINTS OF STORM MANHOLE EXTENSION RINGS SHALL BE RAKED OUT AND ALL EXPOSED FACES SHALL BE LAMINATED WITH EPOXY PAINT. 19. ALL PIPES CONNECTED TO THE MANHOLES ARE TO BE PROVIDED WITH ADEQUATE PUDDLE FLANGES AS REQUIRED. 20. ALL STORM MANHOLES SHALL BE FITTED WITH HEAVY DUTY D400 DI COVERS TO BS EN 124. 21. GRANULAR BED AND SURROUND TO PIPES SHALL BE ENCLOSED IN GEOTEXTILE AS SPECIFIED FOR ALL PIPES. 22. ANY PIPELINE BELOW GROUND LEVEL ENTERING OR PROTRUDING FROM ANY STRUCTURE SHALL BE FITTED WITH TWO FLEXIBLE JOINTS ADJACENT TO THE STRUCTURE AS SPECIFIED UNLESS INDICATED OTHERWISE. 23. CONCRETE SURROUND SHALL BE PROVIDED TO STORMWATER PIPES WHERE THE COVER IS LESS THAN 1.2 METERS. 24. THE OIL INTERCEPTORS SHOWN IN THE DRAWINGS ARE OPTIONAL AND WILL BE USED IN CASE THERE IS NO OIL INTERCEPTOR LOCATED BEFORE THE POND IN THE WADI AREA. 25. INLET TYPE (EITHER CATCH BASIN OR KERB INLET) ARE INDICATIVE FOLLOWING THE DESIGN AND CORRIDORS. IN CASE CONTRACTOR FOUND ON SITE THAT TYPE OF INLET NEEDS TO BE CHANGED FOLLOWING THE ROAD AND SITE CONDITIONS , HE CAN PROCEED ACCORDINGLY. 26. CONTRACTOR TO VERIFY THAT ALL SURFACE LOW POINTS ARE COVERED WITH STORM INLETS ,AND IN CASE NOT COVERED, THE CONTRACTOR TO ADD WHEREVER NEEDED AND CONNECT

THE DESIGN OF THE BOX HAS BEEN BASED ON THE ASSUMPTION THAT THE SOIL UNDER THE BASE OF STRUCTURE HAS A MINIMUM ALLOWABLE BEARING CAPACITY 260kN/m2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CARRY OUT TESTING TO VERIFY THE ABOVE BEARING CAPACITY ON HIS OWN EXPENSE AND NOTIFY THE ENGINEER ACCORDINGLY. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL MAINTAIN AN ACCURATE RECORD OF THE EXCAVATED MATERIAL INCLUDING NATURE OF SOIL AT FORMATION LEVEL AND GROUND WATER. تص ا ريح ال بناء و ال تشييد شهادة اعتماد التصاميم التفصيلية معلومات الشهادة مشروع البنية التحتية لبوابة الدرعية الثانية ال حزمة )االولى (شبكة الصرف الصحي اسم المشروع شهادة اعتماد التصامي م التفصيلية وصف المشروع شركة بوابة الدرعية المحدودة مالك المشروع 03 رقم النسخة 2021220008 رقم الشهادة إعادة إصدار ☒ اصدار جديد ☐ نوع الشهادة 2025/04/14 تاريخ االصدار معلومات المشروع N/A رقم القطعة / بوابة الدرعية2 الحزمة االولى المنطقة شبكة الصرف الصحي نوع المشروع jferreira@diriyah.sa البريد االلكتروني 966 + 552830727 معلومات التواصل جواو فيريرا مقدم الطلب بيانات الفريق الهندسي للمشروع جاكوبس سي إتش تو إم السعودية المحدودة االستشاراي المصمم جاكوبس سي إتش تو إم السعودية المحدودة االستشاري المحلي الشــــروط واألحكـــام 1 . .أي تعديل على هذه الشهادة يلغيها 2 . .ال يسمح بالبدء بأعمال التنفيذ على الموقع قبل الحصول على التصاريح الالزمة من إدارة الشؤون البلدية والتخطيط الحضري 3 . االلتزام بالحصول على موافقة الهيئة قبل القيام بأي تغييرات على التصاميم المنشأة المعتمدة في شهادة موافقة التصاميم أو في أطراف المشروع المعتمدين للم شروع. 4 . .يلتزم المطور والفريق الهندسي للمشروع بالتقيد بجميع أنظمة ولوائح ومعايير واجراءات هيئة تطوير بوابة الدرعية 5 . .يلتزم المطور بالتنسيق وإشعار والحصول على الموافقات الالزمة من الجهات ذات العالقة 6 . .االلتزام باالشتراطات المنصوص عليها في نموذج المراجعة 7 . يقتصر نطاق هذه الشهادة على شبكة مياه الصرف الصحي في البنية التحتية لبوابة الدرعية الثانية الحزمة االولى فقط. ( محطة ضخ مياه الصرف الصحي خارج نطاق هذه الشهادة .) 8 . التأكد من أن جميع الخدمات داخل الممر المخصص لها وعدم وجود تقاطعات. 9 . التأكد من توفير صمامات تحرير الهواء وصمامات الغسيل للتيار الكهربائي الصاعد وفقا لمعايير و متطلبات شركة المياة الوطنية. 10 . التأكد من تنسيق جميع نقاط الواجهات مع جميع البنى التحتية المجاورة بما في ذلك شبكة DG-1 ومنطقة مسك قبل مرحلة البناء . 11 . التأكد من تنسيق جميع نقاط الربط مع المطور و مالك قطعة األرض. 12 . أي هدم للشبكة القائمة يتم تنسيقه مع شركة المياه الوطنية/ مزود الخدمة. 13 . / التأكد من الحصول على شهادة عدم ممانعة موافقات المشغل لشبكة مياه الصرف الصحي قبل مرحلة البناء ال و تأكد من اتباع جميع تعليماته. الختم الرسمي واالعتماد الصورة الجوية للموقع الشؤون البلدية و التخطيط الحضري دييشتلاو ءانبلا حيراصت ةيليصفتلا ميماصتلا د امتعا ةداهش | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ة داهشلا تامولعم | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | )يحصلا فرصلا ةكبش( ىلولاا ةمزحلا ةيناثلا ةيعردلا ةباوبل ةيتحتلا ةينبلا عورشم | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | عورشملا مسا | ةيليصفتلا ميماصتلا دامتعا ةداهش | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | عورشملا فصو | ةدودحملا ةيعردلا ةباوب ةكرش | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | || | | | | | عورشملا كلام | 03 | | |

Information Classification: Public DGII UTILITY IDENTIFICATION SURVEY SCOPE OF WORKS DII UTILITY IDENTIFICATION SURVEY – Scope of Works AECOM Page 2 of 19 Information Classification: Public 1. Overview This document describes the Utility Identification Survey scope of works to be conducted in DII (Area shown in schematic below). The infrastructure package is divided in 3 packages: Package I, Package II and Package III. The below scope of works covers Package I currently but will extend to Packages II and III as optional after agreement with the Client. The information for existing networks for dry and wet utilities has been obtained from the stakeholders/ service providers; however, the accuracy of the information needs to be validated to avoid unforeseen circumstances/ scenarios. This is also fundamental as utility service provisions to existing users will need to be maintained till specific and discrete dates. The existing service connections will be terminated in phases, as the areas become available. The survey should give DGCL a comprehensive picture on the existing utility infrastructure in the highlighted area(s) above which will allow them to identify and quantify to the highest degree of accuracy the amount of utility protection, demolition, diversion needed to carry out the proposed Master Plan in the said zone. DII UTILITY IDENTIFICATION SURVEY – Scope of Works AECOM Page 3 of 19 Information Classification: Public 2. Existing Information The available information for the existing utilities with the Client is included herewith and covers the below. It is to be noted that all the information provided as part of the scope of works is to be treated as ‘For Information Only’. Any text/notes on the drawing not relevant will be ignored. • HV Network (Appendix ‘A’) • MV Network (Appendix ‘B’) • LV Network (Appendix ‘C’) • Telecom Network including GCC Cable (Appendix ‘D’) • Potable Water Network (Appendix ‘E’) • Wastewater Network (Appendix ‘F’) In addition to the above, topographical survey of the area is also available, as ‘For Information Only’, which can be made available to the Contractor upon request. 3. Scope To provide a Complete Utility Identification Survey Report for DII Project Site, based on the following list of minimum works but not limited to: 1- Supervision of the works. The Contractor must ensure to liaise with the Construction Supervision supervising its works to ensure that all procedures are stablished in advance of starting the works. 2- Site Visits. Coordinate and conduct a comprehensive site visit for understanding the client’s requests and needs. The Contractor will ensure full compliance with Safety standards as per Contract. 3- As-Built records/drawings. Before starting works on site, the contractor will endeavour all efforts to secure as much information (as-built records and drawings/ any other relevant information) as possible about all relevant buried and above ground assets to be surveyed, by establishing contact with Authorities and Service Providers and report on its findings accordingly. 4- Pre-condition photographic survey.
